name: Kobo Libra 2
summary: The only device InkHub has ever run on. One development unit and one working unit, both Libra 2.

usb.note: CONFIG_G_DNL_VENDOR_NUM, CONFIG_G_DNL_PRODUCT_NUM and CONFIG_G_DNL_MANUFACTURER in include/configs/mx6sll_ntx_android.h lines 23 to 25. The interface triple is f_fastboot.c lines 54 to 56. Field-confirmed on 2026-08-30, docs/kernel-boot-experiments.md section 11.

entry.title: Put the Libra 2 into fastboot
steps: Plug the cable directly into this computer. Not through a hub: the bootloader's USB gadget does not survive one.
Short-press power, and keep holding the top button through the first seconds.
warnings: Do not hold power together with a page key. That is Kobo's factory-restore gesture and it erases the device.
If nothing appears within about 40 seconds, power cycle and try again. A failed enumeration burns nothing.

checks.label: USB identity
checks.why: The vendor, product and interface triple this bootloader's fastboot gadget reports. Chrome filters on the first two before the device is even offered.

checks.name: version
checks.why: The fastboot protocol version this U-Boot answers. Read off the wire on 2026-08-30. Weak on its own, and it is here to catch a device that is answering fastboot but is not this bootloader.

checks.name: max-download-size
checks.why: CONFIG_FASTBOOT_BUF_SIZE, 400 MiB. Confirmed from the wire. Every payload here is sent in one shot and must fit under it.

checks.name: hwcfg.PCB
checks.why: The board revision byte, hwconfig offset 16. This is the same byte the on-device gate checks, and it is the row docs/second-device.md marks must match exactly. Nothing checks it before a fastboot write, so an install refuses if the bootloader will not answer it.

checks.name: hwcfg.DisplayResolution
checks.why: 16 is 1680x1264, the ED070KH3 panel. The panel timings in this device tree are that panel's.

checks.name: serialno
checks.why: Recorded for the log, never gated on. It is the SoC serial printed as two decimal numbers, and it differs on every device.

unreadable: getvar all, product, serial and every partition-* query answer FAILVariable not implemented. The identity this page can read is the four hwcfg values above and nothing else.
Fastboot has no read command at all, so nothing written can be read back from the browser, and no backup can be taken.

The panel VCOM, the waveform id and the waveform mode version are all rows docs/second-device.md marks must match exactly, and none of them is reachable over fastboot. They are checked on the device by mainline/rootfs/usr/sbin/libra2-vcom, which refuses to bring the display up if it cannot read them.
unwritable: Sector 1285, the device tree slot's NTX header. It is the magic U-Boot checks on every boot, and it falls in the gap between the ntxfw target (1030 to 1284) and the dtb target (1286 to 1535). No fastboot target covers it, so the browser cannot write it and cannot complete an install on its own.

live.note: The whole system, RAM-booted. The image runs the same board gate and reads the same per-panel calibration an installed system does, so a live session that comes up is direct evidence that the identity gate passes on this hardware.

writes.label: the system partition
writes.note: rootfs is the fastboot name for p1. The MBR partitions register as rootfs (p1), recoveryfs (p2) and vfat (p3); this writes the first and never the other two.

writes.label: the kernel
writes.note: The raw slot from sector 2048. On the Kobo branch the loader reads a fixed 11264 sectors and never looks at a header, so the payload is a bare zImage.

writes.label: the device tree
writes.note: The raw slot from sector 1286. This is the body only. Its header sector is one sector lower and out of reach.

writes.label: the last sector, on the device
writes.note: A RAM-booted payload that reads the three slots back, writes sector 1285 last, and says on the panel whether every read-back matched. It is the only way the boot gate gets written and the only read-back this route has.

release.note: manifest.json is the name tools/release.sh publishes and mainline/rootfs/usr/sbin/libra2-update fetches. assetBase is a same-origin path: GitHub sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin on release downloads, so the page cannot fetch them cross-origin, and vercel.json routes /dl/ through this site. Point assetBase at upstream only on a host that serves CORS headers for it.

live.label: InkHub Live
live.note: out/phase2/live/fastboot-live.img, sent whole and RAM-booted. Nothing is written.

rootfs.label: the system partition
rootfs.note: The bundle's own p1.ext4.xz cannot be used here: no browser has xz, and the pieces inside the tar have no URL of their own. So the release publishes a gzip copy as its own asset, because DecompressionStream('gzip') is already in every browser that has WebUSB. Its webp1_plain_sha256 is the hash of the unpacked image, which the finisher reads back against.

kernel.label: the kernel
kernel.note: The bare zImage, NOT the bundle's kernel-slot.img. kernel-slot.img carries the sector 2047 header in front of the kernel and the fastboot kernel target starts at 2048, so sending it here would shift the whole image by one sector. The Kobo branch of the loader never reads that header sector.

dtb.label: the device tree
dtb.note: The body only. The bundle's dtb-hdr.bin has no fastboot target to go to: see unwritable above.

finisher.label: the finisher
finisher.note: Does not exist yet. Until a release carries it, this page cannot complete an install and says so rather than doing three quarters of one.

finish.title: Now power-cycle the device by hand
steps: Hold the power button for about 20 seconds, until the screen changes.
Let go, then press power again to switch the device back on.
finish.expect: Within about a minute, the launcher's home screen: portrait, page keys on the right, the app tiles, and the version along the bottom.

recovery.gesture: Hold power and a page key together for ten seconds. That is Kobo's factory restore. It rewrites the bootloader environment, the kernel slot and the device tree from the recovery partition and reformats p1 and p3, so the device is a stock Kobo again at the cost of the books on it.
recovery.untouched: This flow never writes the bootloader, the environment block, the hwconfig record, the serial number, the waveform, the recovery partition p2 or the FAT partition p3. Your books are on p3.
